text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt decided not to attend the summit called by U.S. President Bill Clinton to discuss ways to save the peace process in the Middle East. President Hosni Mubarak earlier discussed the summit with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif said Mubarak encouraged Arafat to take part in the summit because he trusts President Clinton's word.
-- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa will not take in the summit but he will cooperate with Arafat.
- CNN said Mubarak played an important role in the peace process and no doubt wanted to continue to play such a role.

- The Minister of Housing and New Communities, Mohamed Ibrahim Soleiman, said that 56 million square metres of land have been set aside in new towns for individuals, associations and private sector companies.
- The Nile waters in Lake Nasser are only 21 centimetres short of the Toshka overflow canal.
- At a three-hour meeting in Alexandria, Mubarak made great efforts to convince Arafat that he must attend the Washington summit to put and defend the Palestinian point of view.

- Front-page editorial by Galal Duweidar says the Washington summit will be useless unless it pushes the peace process in the right direction, based on legitimate rights, agreements and U.N. resolutions.
- In Beni Suef the Sheikh of al-Azhar says that Israel's latest measures are criminal and inflammatory.

- Strange wild animals are descending on the southern town of Armint from the mountains and attacking people. Four people have been killed and 18 injured so far. People have not been able to identify the species.
- Mubarak will not take part in the summit because of his prior engagements.
- The new Shubra-Ramses line of the Cairo underground will open this morning.

- Front-page editorial says the Egyptian government did well to ask for the Washington summit to be postponed because to hold it under these circumstances, without good preparation or any definite Israeli commitment, will help to aggravate the crisis and give Netanyahu a chance to escape from the dilemma he created through his stupidity, obstinacy and contempt for international charters.
